endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Define key concepts in the AI Policy (e.g., definition of AI, scope of AI solution use, AI approval process).

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Establish terms of use and terms of service for GAI systems.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbots in Medicine: A Supplement, Not a Substitute
endorsements.quote: Ethical considerations extend to ensuring transparency in chatbot interactions, obtaining proper consent for data collection and use, and establishing clear guidelines for chatbot use in clinical settings to prevent misuse or misinterpretation.

commentary.bottom_line: Four sources endorse publishing permitted and prohibited uses and keeping a misuse mitigation plan, but no supplied study tests whether the practice reduces misuse or shows how often staff misuse AI. The recommendation rests on expert consensus from three frameworks and one commentary.

perspectives.view: No supplied study evaluates this practice, and no supplied study documents how often the targeted hazard occurs. The support consists of three frameworks and one commentary, which GRADE treats as expert opinion rather than evidence. Certainty about whether published use rules reduce prohibited or off-label use cannot be rated.

CHAI rates defining the scope of AI solution use as a must, while NIST AI 600-1 and the CHAI Assurance Standards Guide rate terms of use and misuse mitigation plans as should. These are voluntary frameworks. The supplied material does not tie the practice to a binding FDA, ONC, or state requirement.

The supplied material contains no incident data showing staff misuse of AI or the harm that follows. Without hazard or outcome studies, the panel cannot judge whether a published list of prohibited uses would stop errors before they reach patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies should measure how often staff use deployed AI tools outside their approved scope, and compare rates of off-label or prohibited use before and after governance bodies publish use rules and misuse mitigation plans. Such studies should also examine whether staff read and follow the published rules and what enforcement mechanisms accompany them.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these patients have no evidence on whether misuse differs in their settings or whether published use rules protect their patients.
